text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing swelling in your right knee and have a family history of similar issues; could you describe exactly when the swelling started and what activities triggered it?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor

DIAGNOSIS READY: NOT READY (Insufficient clinical data).

Thank you for the details; given the patient is an 18-month-old with spontaneous swelling and a family history, this raises concern for conditions like Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease, synovial chondromatosis, or early-onset inflammatory arthritis. To proceed, please describe the knee's range of motion and any limitation in walking or weight-bearing. REQUEST IMAGES: Right knee X-ray (AP and Lateral views).
